title: Carranza v. Mercedes-Benz USA LLC
citation: 2021 WL 4805198 (C.D. Cal. 2021), as cited in the assigned problem
lead: An automobile problem asks whether a manufacturer outside the retail sales contract can enforce its arbitration clause; the available assignment supplies the question, not a verified judicial answer.

sections.title: The car passes from manufacturer to dealer to customer
sections.cue: Where is the arbitration promise made?
paragraphs: The textbook’s problem describes a customer buying an automobile from a dealer. The dealer had obtained the car from the manufacturer. The customer’s sales agreement with the dealer contains a mandatory arbitration clause.

Those are two separate commercial relationships. The agreement described as containing the arbitration promise is the retail agreement between the customer and dealer, not an identified agreement signed by the manufacturer.

sections.title: Problems with the car lead to a suit against its manufacturer
sections.cue: Why does the identity of the defendant matter?
paragraphs: After problems with the car, the customer sues the manufacturer. The assignment does not describe the particular defects, reproduce the complaint or set out the arbitration clause beyond stating that it is mandatory.

The defendant’s connection to the product is clear, but it remains outside the customer–dealer contract described in the problem. That difference creates the question about who may enforce the contract’s arbitration promise.

sections.title: The problem asks whether beneficiary status supports enforcement
sections.cue: What argument must the reader evaluate?
paragraphs: The editors ask whether the manufacturer can claim intended-beneficiary status under the customer–dealer agreement and compel arbitration. They cite Carranza v. Mercedes-Benz USA LLC as the decision to consult.

The question calls for examination of the agreement’s language, who was intended to benefit, and the requirements for enforcement by a nonsignatory. The excerpt itself neither answers those questions nor establishes that the actual defendant made or prevailed on that particular argument.

sections.title: The available account ends before a verified court ruling
paragraphs: The complete cited decision has not been recovered in the available materials. There is therefore no verified order compelling or refusing arbitration, no established intended-beneficiary holding, and no resolution of alternative enforcement theories to recount.

The citation printed in the assignment is 2021 WL 4805198. The assigned scenario identifies the contract-enforcement question for study, while the actual parties’ facts, full clause and judicial disposition remain unresolved.
